question: A square playground has sides of length $18\text{ m}$. Calculate the perimeter of the playground.
working: Perimeter of a square = 4 × side length = 4 × 18 = 72 m.

topic: Perimeter of rectilinear shapes in $\text{cm}$ and $\text{m}$

question: An L-shaped rectilinear room has six sides. Starting from the top horizontal edge and going clockwise, the side lengths are $9\text{ m}$, $4\text{ m}$, $3\text{ m}$, $5\text{ m}$, $6\text{ m}$, and $9\text{ m}$. What is the perimeter of the room?
working: Perimeter = sum of all outer sides = 9 + 4 + 3 + 5 + 6 + 9 = 36 m.

topic: Perimeter of rectilinear shapes in $\text{cm}$ and $\text{m}$

question: The perimeter of a square tile is $36\text{ cm}$. What is the length of one side of the tile?
working: Side length = Perimeter ÷ 4 = 36 ÷ 4 = 9 cm.

topic: Perimeter of rectilinear shapes in $\text{cm}$ and $\text{m}$
subtopic: Perimeter of rectilinear shapes in cm and m
question: An L-shaped rectilinear shape has a total horizontal width of $12\text{ cm}$ along the bottom and a total vertical height of $10\text{ cm}$ on the left. The top horizontal edge is $7\text{ cm}$ and the far right vertical edge is $4\text{ cm}$. Calculate the perimeter of the shape.
working: Missing inner horizontal edge = 12 - 7 = 5 cm. Missing inner vertical edge = 10 - 4 = 6 cm. Perimeter = 12 + 10 + 7 + 4 + 5 + 6 = 44 cm.

topic: Perimeter of rectilinear shapes in $\text{cm}$ and $\text{m}$
subtopic: Perimeter of rectilinear shapes in cm and m
question: A rectangle has a perimeter of $48\text{ cm}$. Its length is $16\text{ cm}$. What is the width of the rectangle?
working: Sum of two lengths = 16 × 2 = 32 cm. Sum of two widths = 48 - 32 = 16 cm. Width = 16 ÷ 2 = 8 cm.

topic: Perimeter of rectilinear shapes in $\text{cm}$ and $\text{m}$
subtopic: Perimeter of rectilinear shapes in cm and m
question: A rectilinear garden has an overall length of $15\text{ m}$ along the bottom and an overall height of $11\text{ m}$ along the left side. The top edge is $8\text{ m}$ and the right-hand edge is $6\text{ m}$. A corner is indented with two inner perpendicular edges. What is the total perimeter of the garden?
working: The missing horizontal edge = 15 - 8 = 7 m. The missing vertical edge = 11 - 6 = 5 m. Perimeter = 15 + 11 + 8 + 5 + 7 + 6 = 52 m.

topic: Perimeter of rectilinear shapes in $\text{cm}$ and $\text{m}$
subtopic: Perimeter of rectilinear shapes in cm and m
question: Shape A is a rectangle measuring $9\text{ m}$ by $5\text{ m}$. Shape B is a square with the exact same perimeter as Shape A. What is the length of one side of Shape B?
working: Perimeter of Shape A = (9 + 5) × 2 = 28 m. Side length of Shape B = 28 ÷ 4 = 7 m.

topic: Perimeter of rectilinear shapes in $\text{cm}$ and $\text{m}$
subtopic: Perimeter of rectilinear shapes in cm and m
question: Two identical rectangles, each with a length of $12\text{ cm}$ and a width of $5\text{ cm}$, are joined end-to-end along their shorter sides to make one longer rectangle. What is the perimeter of the new shape?
working: New length = 12 + 12 = 24 cm. New width = 5 cm. Perimeter = (24 + 5) × 2 = 29 × 2 = 58 cm.

topic: Perimeter of rectilinear shapes in $\text{cm}$ and $\text{m}$
subtopic: Perimeter of rectilinear shapes in cm and m
question: A rectilinear shape is made by placing a small square with sides of $4\text{ cm}$ on top of a rectangle measuring $10\text{ cm}$ by $6\text{ cm}$, so that one side of the square rests along the middle of the $10\text{ cm}$ top side. What is the perimeter of the combined rectilinear shape?
working: Perimeter of rectangle = (10 + 6) × 2 = 32 cm. Adding the square adds 3 of its sides (3 × 4 = 12 cm) but covers 1 side (4 cm) on the rectangle: 32 + 12 - 4 = 40 cm.

topic: Area of rectilinear shapes by counting squares
subtopic: Area of rectilinear shapes by counting squares
question: A rectilinear shape is drawn on a grid of centimetre squares. It is completely filled by 9 whole squares. What is the area of the shape?
working: Each square on the grid has an area of 1 cm². Since the shape contains 9 whole squares, the total area is 9 × 1 cm² = 9 cm².

topic: Area of rectilinear shapes by counting squares
subtopic: Area of rectilinear shapes by counting squares
question: A rectangle is drawn on a grid of 1 cm² squares. It has 4 rows with 3 squares in each row. What is the total area of the rectangle?
working: Count the total number of centimetre squares: 4 rows of 3 squares = 4 × 3 = 12 squares. The area is 12 cm².

topic: Area of rectilinear shapes by counting squares
subtopic: Area of rectilinear shapes by counting squares
question: An L-shaped rectilinear figure on a centimetre grid is made of a vertical column of 6 squares and a horizontal row of 2 squares attached at the bottom right. What is the area of this L-shaped figure in square centimetres?
working: Count all the squares that make up the rectilinear figure: 6 squares + 2 squares = 8 squares. Each square is 1 cm², so the total area is 8 cm².

topic: Area of rectilinear shapes by counting squares
subtopic: Area of rectilinear shapes by counting squares
question: A T-shaped rectilinear shape is drawn on a grid where each square is 1 cm². The horizontal top bar is made of 7 squares. The vertical section underneath the middle square is made of 4 squares. What is the total area of the shape?
working: Total squares = 7 (top bar) + 4 (vertical section) = 11 squares. Since each square is 1 cm², the total area is 11 cm².

topic: Area of rectilinear shapes by counting squares
subtopic: Area of rectilinear shapes by counting squares
question: Shape A covers 14 squares on a 1 cm² grid. Shape B covers 19 squares on the same grid. How many square centimetres larger is the area of Shape B than Shape A?
working: Area of Shape A = 14 cm². Area of Shape B = 19 cm². Difference = 19 cm² - 14 cm² = 5 cm².

topic: Area of rectilinear shapes by counting squares
subtopic: Area of rectilinear shapes by counting squares
question: A shaded shape on a centimetre squared grid is made of 11 full squares and 4 half-squares. What is the total area of the shape in cm²?
working: 4 half-squares = 4 ÷ 2 = 2 full squares. Total full squares = 11 + 2 = 13 squares. Therefore, the area is 13 cm².

topic: Area of rectilinear shapes by counting squares
subtopic: Area of rectilinear shapes by counting squares
question: A rectilinear shape on a grid of 1 cm² squares is made from two non-overlapping rectangles joined together. The first rectangle contains 3 rows of 5 squares. The second rectangle contains 2 rows of 4 squares. What is the total area of the rectilinear shape?
working: First rectangle = 3 × 5 = 15 squares = 15 cm². Second rectangle = 2 × 4 = 8 squares = 8 cm². Total area = 15 cm² + 8 cm² = 23 cm².

topic: Area of rectilinear shapes by counting squares
subtopic: Area of rectilinear shapes by counting squares
question: A large square on a grid of centimetre squares measures 5 squares by 5 squares. A smaller square measuring 2 squares by 2 squares is removed from one corner. What is the area of the remaining rectilinear shape?
working: Area of large square = 5 × 5 = 25 cm². Area of removed square = 2 × 2 = 4 cm². Area of remaining shape = 25 cm² - 4 cm² = 21 cm².

topic: Area of rectilinear shapes by counting squares
subtopic: Area of rectilinear shapes by counting squares
question: On a grid of 1 cm² squares, Shape X is a rectangle made of 4 rows of 6 squares. Shape Y is a square made of 5 rows of 5 squares. Which shape has the greater area and by how many cm²?
working: Area of Shape X = 4 × 6 = 24 cm². Area of Shape Y = 5 × 5 = 25 cm². Shape Y is larger by 25 - 24 = 1 cm².

topic: Area of rectilinear shapes by counting squares
subtopic: Area of rectilinear shapes by counting squares
question: Hannah is drawing a rectilinear shape with a total area of 28 cm² on a 1 cm² grid. She has already shaded 19 squares. How many more whole squares does she need to shade to complete the shape?
working: Target area = 28 squares. Shaded so far = 19 squares. Remaining squares to shade = 28 - 19 = 9 squares.

topic: Area of rectilinear shapes by counting squares
subtopic: Area of rectilinear shapes by counting squares
question: A cross-shaped rectilinear tile pattern on a grid of 1 m² squares consists of a central square of 4 squares (2 by 2), with an extra block of 2 squares attached to each of its 4 outer sides. What is the total area of the pattern in square metres?
working: Central square = 2 × 2 = 4 squares. Four outer blocks = 4 × 2 = 8 squares. Total squares = 4 + 8 = 12 squares. Since each square is 1 m², the total area is 12 m².

topic: Area of rectilinear shapes by counting squares
subtopic: Area of rectilinear shapes by counting squares
question: A rectilinear picture frame drawn on a centimetre grid has an outer boundary of 7 squares by 6 squares. The empty space in the middle is 4 squares by 3 squares. Counting the squares of the border, what is the area of the picture frame in cm²?
working: Total outer area = 7 × 6 = 42 squares. Inner empty area = 4 × 3 = 12 squares. Area of the frame = 42 - 12 = 30 squares = 30 cm².

topic: Time conversions (hr/min/sec, yr/mth, wk/day) and 12h/24h durations

question: Leo spends 150 seconds brushing his teeth. Maya spends 2 minutes and 40 seconds brushing her teeth. How many seconds longer does Maya spend brushing her teeth than Leo?
working: Convert Maya's time to seconds: 2 minutes 40 seconds = (2 × 60) + 40 = 120 + 40 = 160 seconds. Difference: 160 - 150 = 10 seconds.

topic: Time conversions (hr/min/sec, yr/mth, wk/day) and 12h/24h durations
question: A tree in the school garden is 5 years old. How many months old is the tree?
working: There are 12 months in 1 year. 5 × 12 = 60 months.

topic: Time conversions (hr/min/sec, yr/mth, wk/day) and 12h/24h durations
question: A building project took 36 months to finish. How many years is this?
working: There are 12 months in 1 year. 36 ÷ 12 = 3 years.

topic: Time conversions (hr/min/sec, yr/mth, wk/day) and 12h/24h durations
question: An elephant calf is 2 years and 7 months old. What is the calf's age in months?
working: 2 years = 2 × 12 = 24 months. 24 + 7 = 31 months.

topic: Time conversions (hr/min/sec, yr/mth, wk/day) and 12h/24h durations
question: A car lease lasts for 50 months. Convert 50 months into years and months.
working: 50 ÷ 12 = 4 with a remainder of 2 (since 4 × 12 = 48). 50 months = 4 years and 2 months.

topic: Time conversions (hr/min/sec, yr/mth, wk/day) and 12h/24h durations
question: A summer camp lasts for 6 weeks. How many days does the camp last?
working: There are 7 days in 1 week. 6 × 7 = 42 days.

topic: Time conversions (hr/min/sec, yr/mth, wk/day) and 12h/24h durations
question: There are 56 days until sports day. How many weeks is this?
working: There are 7 days in 1 week. 56 ÷ 7 = 8 weeks.

topic: Time conversions (hr/min/sec, yr/mth, wk/day) and 12h/24h durations
question: A family goes on holiday for 3 weeks and 4 days. How many days are they on holiday in total?
working: 3 weeks = 3 × 7 = 21 days. 21 + 4 = 25 days.

topic: Time conversions (hr/min/sec, yr/mth, wk/day) and 12h/24h durations
question: A bird's eggs take 38 days to hatch. Convert 38 days into weeks and days.
working: 38 ÷ 7 = 5 with a remainder of 3 (since 5 × 7 = 35). 38 days = 5 weeks and 3 days.

topic: Time conversions (hr/min/sec, yr/mth, wk/day) and 12h/24h durations
question: A train departs at 4:35 pm. Write this time using the 24-hour clock.
working: To convert a pm time to 24-hour format, add 12 to the hour: 4 + 12 = 16. The time is 16:35.

topic: Time conversions (hr/min/sec, yr/mth, wk/day) and 12h/24h durations
question: A digital clock shows the time 20:15. Write this time using the 12-hour clock, including am or pm.
working: 20 - 12 = 8, so 20:15 in 12-hour format is 8:15 pm.

topic: Time conversions (hr/min/sec, yr/mth, wk/day) and 12h/24h durations
question: A school assembly begins at 9:20 am. Write this time as a 24-hour digital clock time.
working: For morning times before 10:00 am, include a leading zero: 9:20 am becomes 09:20.

topic: Time conversions (hr/min/sec, yr/mth, wk/day) and 12h/24h durations
question: A football match starts at 14:15 and finishes at 16:00. How many minutes does the match last?
working: From 14:15 to 15:00 is 45 minutes. From 15:00 to 16:00 is 60 minutes. 45 + 60 = 105 minutes.

topic: Time conversions (hr/min/sec, yr/mth, wk/day) and 12h/24h durations
question: A concert ends at 21:40. The concert lasted for 1 hour and 25 minutes. At what time did the concert start? Give your answer using the 24-hour clock.
working: Subtract 1 hour: 21:40 - 1 hour = 20:40. Subtract 25 minutes: 20:40 - 25 minutes = 20:15.

topic: Time conversions (hr/min/sec, yr/mth, wk/day) and 12h/24h durations
question: A bus journey begins at 11:35 am and takes 50 minutes. At what time does the bus journey finish? Give your answer in 12-hour time, including am or pm.
working: 11:35 am + 25 minutes = 12:00 pm (noon). 12:00 pm + 25 minutes = 12:25 pm.

question: In a pictogram showing the number of books read by different classes, each symbol of an open book represents 8 books. Class 4B has 4 whole book symbols and 1 half book symbol. How many books did Class 4B read?
working: 1 whole symbol = 8 books. 4 whole symbols = 4 × 8 = 32 books. 1 half symbol = 8 ÷ 2 = 4 books. Total = 32 + 4 = 36 books.

question: A pictogram shows the number of visitors to a wildlife park. The key shows that 1 full circle represents 12 visitors. On Friday, the pictogram shows 3 whole circles and 1 quarter circle. How many visitors were there on Friday?
working: 1 whole circle = 12 visitors. 3 whole circles = 3 × 12 = 36 visitors. 1 quarter circle = 12 ÷ 4 = 3 visitors. Total = 36 + 3 = 39 visitors.

question: In a school survey about favourite fruits, 1 apple symbol represents 8 children. Apples: 3 whole symbols and 1 half symbol. Bananas: 5 whole symbols and 1 quarter symbol. How many more children chose bananas than apples?
working: Children who chose apples = (3 × 8) + (8 ÷ 2) = 24 + 4 = 28. Children who chose bananas = (5 × 8) + (8 ÷ 4) = 40 + 2 = 42. Difference = 42 - 28 = 14.

question: A line graph tracks the temperature of water cooling in a science experiment over four recordings: at 0 minutes it was 80°C, at 5 minutes it was 62°C, at 10 minutes it was 48°C, and at 15 minutes it was 35°C. At which recorded time was the water temperature closest to 50°C?
working: Find the difference from 50°C for each recording: 80 - 50 = 30°C; 62 - 50 = 12°C; 50 - 48 = 2°C; 50 - 35 = 15°C. The smallest difference is 2°C at 10 minutes.

question: A table shows the number of swimmers at a leisure centre across four sessions on Saturday: Morning session had 145 swimmers, Midday session had 218 swimmers, Afternoon session had 264 swimmers, and Evening session had 183 swimmers. What was the total number of swimmers across all four sessions?
working: 145 + 218 + 264 + 183 = 810 swimmers in total.

question: A pictogram shows the number of trees planted by a conservation group over three weeks. The key shows that 1 tree symbol represents 40 trees. Week 1 has 3 symbols, Week 2 has 4 symbols, and Week 3 has 2 and a half symbols. How many trees were planted altogether over the three weeks?
working: Week 1: 3 × 40 = 120 trees. Week 2: 4 × 40 = 160 trees. Week 3: (2 × 40) + 20 = 100 trees. Total = 120 + 160 + 100 = 380 trees.

question: A bar chart shows the number of books loaned by a community library: 186 books on Monday, 245 books on Tuesday, 198 books on Wednesday, and 312 books on Thursday. How many more books were loaned on Thursday than on Monday?

question: A pictogram shows the number of merit stickers earned by two classes. The key states that 1 star symbol represents 8 stickers. Class 4R has 7 whole star symbols. Class 4S has 4 whole star symbols and 1 half star symbol. How many more stickers did Class 4R earn than Class 4S?
working: Class 4R: 7 × 8 = 56 stickers. Class 4S: (4 × 8) + 4 = 36 stickers. Difference: 56 - 36 = 20 stickers.
